claims.text: Introducing Ti- and Ni-rich, coherently embedded L12 precipitates into an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix will restore the orbital magnetic moment.
The L12 precipitates will induce strong magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The proposed dual-phase alloy will achieve coercivity exceeding 100 Oe significantly above room temperature.
Coherent L12 precipitation can preserve an fcc matrix.
A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has suppressed orbital moments and low coercivity because of the high symmetry and isotropic nature of the fcc lattice.
Annealing at 900–950 °C can induce nanoscale, coherent L12 precipitates in an fcc high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The annealing treatment will specifically produce Ni3Ti or Ni3(Fe,Co,Ti) precipitates in Fe-Co-Ni-Ti.
The fcc matrix will remain stable and the L12 precipitates will retain order from 300 K to 600 K.
L12 precipitates break local cubic symmetry in the surrounding matrix.
Coherent L12 precipitates introduce strain fields.
L12 precipitates and their strain fields act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
Chemical ordering and local symmetry breaking restore an orbital-moment contribution suppressed in the disordered fcc phase.
Coherent-interface stress fields increase the energy barrier for magnetic-domain reversal and thereby raise coercivity.
The mechanical particle-strengthening mechanism of L12 precipitates can be transferred to magnetic-domain pinning.
The alloy will show square magnetic hysteresis loops indicative of strong anisotropy.
Coherent precipitates will maintain high ductility and strength in the fcc matrix.
The single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti baseline has coercivity below 10 Oe.
Heusler or B2 phases may form as competing intermetallic phases rather than the intended coherent L12 precipitates.
Exceeding a precipitate-volume-fraction threshold will embrittle the matrix and change deformation from dislocation glide to brittle fracture.
Thermally induced magnetic moments and magnetic-entropy effects in CoCrFeMnNi provide evidence for L12-order-induced orbital-moment restoration in Fe-Co-Ni-Ti.

contradictions.description: The conditions characterize 300–600 K as significantly above room temperature, while the predicted threshold is stated only for temperatures above 300 K; 300 K itself is approximately room temperature.

The predicted coercivity threshold applies at temperatures above 300 K, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis if coercivity is below 100 Oe at any temperature up to 500 K, potentially including 300 K and unspecified lower temperatures outside the prediction.

Precipitate incoherency or transformation is defined as outside the hypothesis's applicability boundary, but the falsification rule treats those failed intervention conditions as falsification of the hypothesis itself.
